summary:
# Week 4: The Empire Strikes Back (and cosmohouck IS the Empire)

Folks, cosmohouck just delivered a 169.96-point atomic elbow drop that would make Thanos proud – perfectly balanced destruction. That 99.94-point beatdown of powerperson? That's not a fantasy matchup, that's the Red Wedding from Game of Thrones. Tetairoa McMillan went full Super Saiyan with 38.2 points while Kenneth Walker added 30.4, and somewhere powerperson is still looking for survivors in the rubble. Meanwhile, powerperson trotted out Tyler Shough and Cam Ward at QB like they were auditioning for a buddy cop movie nobody asked for, combining for 31.5 points – cute, but you brought water pistols to a Death Star fight. Michael Pittman's 2.5 points? That's the fantasy equivalent of showing up to the Avengers with a pointy stick.

The PrinceofPizza versus TophTT showdown was like watching two heavyweight boxers actually land punches – 162.04 to 129.46, the kind of scoring that makes you check if someone accidentally added an extra digit. Puka Nacua (23.2) and Zay Flowers (21.8) turned PrinceofPizza into an offensive fireworks display, while TophTT's Javonte Williams rumbled for 28.8 points in what I can only describe as the fantasy equivalent of John Wick fighting his way through an entire nightclub. Both teams scored enough to win 90% of matchups this week, but somebody had to lose – that's fantasy football doing its best Highlander impression: there can be only one.

Shogunation's CeeDee Lamb absolutely went off for 32.8 points like he was auditioning for the role of "guy who single-handedly carries entire franchise" – and he got it. But here's the plot twist worthy of The Sixth Sense: Saquon Barkley, the guy you probably drafted in the first two rounds, delivered a soul-crushing 1.5 points. ONE POINT FIVE! That's not a running back performance, that's a typo. Travis Kelce added 2.5 points, meaning Shogunation's two premium assets combined for four points while probably costing 30% of the draft budget. It's like buying a Ferrari and a Lamborghini, then taking the bus to work. Still won by 43, though, because CeeDee decided to be the entire Dallas offense.

And can we talk about mjgrana's "The Burrow-Williams Connection" pulling off the comeback special? Down in the power rankings at #3 versus mastab24's #9 position, Kyren Williams (31.7) and Joe Burrow (23.7) combined like peanut butter and chocolate – a combination so good it makes you wonder why you ever doubted it. Mastab24, bless their heart, started Rashee Rice who delivered a perfect 0.0 – and based on those lineup decisions, they apparently left nearly 36 points on the bench. That's not roster management, that's fantasy self-sabotage. That's like having Indiana Jones's whip and choosing to bring a pool noodle instead. The "Bench Warmer General" mastab24 snatched defeat from the jaws of... well, probably still defeat, but at least make it competitive!
